question: List every release in the changelog of charset-normalizer.
answer:
### [3.5.3](https://github.com/Ousret/charset_normalizer/compare/3.5.2...3.5.3) (2026-11-23)
- Faster noise scoring in both the pure-Python and Cython implementations by reusing Unicode character properties. [15]
- Cython extensions also speed up language ranking and checks for suspicious transitions between Unicode blocks [15].

### [3.5.2](https://github.com/Ousret/charset_normalizer/compare/3.5.1...3.5.2) (2026-09-29)
- Raised the Cython upper bound to `<3.4` for native builds. [16]
- The bound remains `<3.3` for `abi3` builds to preserve compatibility with the Python 3.7 Limited API [16].

### [3.5.1](https://github.com/Ousret/charset_normalizer/compare/3.5.0...3.5.1) (2026-08-15)
- Raised upper bound of setuptools to v84 (#794). [17]
- Cache performance access optimization for our CharInfo struct (prebuilt only) [17].

### [3.5.0](https://github.com/Ousret/charset_normalizer/compare/3.4.9...3.5.0) (2026-08-12)
- Explicit support for Python 3.15 [18].

### [3.4.9](https://github.com/Ousret/charset_normalizer/compare/3.4.8...3.4.9) (2026-07-07)
- Regression in our fallback path leading to a decode error. (#771) We've yanked 3.4.8 as a result of that bug [19].

### [3.4.8](https://github.com/Ousret/charset_normalizer/compare/3.4.7...3.4.8) (2026-07-06)
- Wall import time due to cascade codec imports for our multibyte first sort of iana supported codecs (#742). [20]
- Unnecessary json import at runtime (#753). [20]
- Inverse capitalization not seen by noise detector (#731) [20].

### [3.4.7](https://github.com/Ousret/charset_normalizer/compare/3.4.6...3.4.7) (2026-04-02)
- Pre-built optimized version using mypy[c] v1.20. [21]
- Relax `setuptools` constraint to `setuptools>=68,<82.1` [21].

### [3.4.6](https://github.com/Ousret/charset_normalizer/compare/3.4.5...3.4.6) (2026-03-15)
- Flattened the logic in `charset_normalizer.md` for higher performance. Removed `eligible(..)` and `feed(...) ` in favor of `feed_info(...)`. [22]
- Raised upper bound for mypy[c] to 1.20, for our optimized version. [22]
- Updated … [22]

### [3.4.5](https://github.com/Ousret/charset_normalizer/compare/3.4.4...3.4.5) (2026-03-06)
- Update `setuptools` constraint to `setuptools>=68,<=82`. [23]
- Raised upper bound of mypyc for the optional pre-built extension to v1.19.1 [23]

### [3.4.4](https://github.com/Ousret/charset_normalizer/compare/3.4.2...3.4.4) (2025-10-13)
- Bound `setuptools` to a specific constraint `setuptools>=68,<=81`. [24]
- Raised upper bound of mypyc for the optional pre-built extension to v1.18.2 [24]

### [3.4.3](https://github.com/Ousret/charset_normalizer/compare/3.4.2...3.4.3) (2025-08-09)
- mypy(c) is no longer a required dependency at build time if `CHARSET_NORMALIZER_USE_MYPYC` isn't set to `1`. (#595) (#583) [25]
- automatically lower confidence on small bytes samples that are not Unicode in `detect` output legacy function. [25]

### [3.4.2](https://github.com/Ousret/charset_normalizer/compare/3.4.1...3.4.2) (2025-05-02)
- Addressed the DeprecationWarning in our CLI regarding `argparse.FileType` by backporting the target class into the package. (#591) [26]
- Improved the overall reliability of the detector with CJK Ideographs. (#605) (#587) [26]

### [3.4.1](https://github.com/Ousret/charset_normalizer/compare/3.4.0...3.4.1) (2024-12-24)
- Project metadata are now stored using `pyproject.toml` instead of `setup.cfg` using setuptools as the build backend. [27]
- Enforce annotation delayed loading for a simpler and consistent types in the project. [27]
- Optional mypyc compilation … [27]

### [3.4.0](https://github.com/Ousret/charset_normalizer/compare/3.3.2...3.4.0) (2024-10-08)
- Argument `--no-preemptive` in the CLI to prevent the detector to search for hints. [28]
- Support for Python 3.13 (#512) [28]

### [3.3.2](https://github.com/Ousret/charset_normalizer/compare/3.3.1...3.3.2) (2023-10-31)
- Unintentional memory usage regression when using large payload that match several encoding (#376) [29]
- Regression on some detection case showcased in the documentation (#371) [29]

### [3.3.1](https://github.com/Ousret/charset_normalizer/compare/3.3.0...3.3.1) (2023-10-22)
- Optional mypyc compilation upgraded to version 1.6.1 for Python >= 3.8 [30]
- Improved the general detection reliability based on reports from the community [30]

### [3.3.0](https://github.com/Ousret/charset_normalizer/compare/3.2.0...3.3.0) (2023-09-30)
- Allow to execute the CLI (e.g. normalizer) through `python -m charset_normalizer.cli` or `python -m charset_normalizer` [31]
- Support for 9 forgotten encoding that are supported by Python but unlisted in `encoding.aliases` as they have no [31]

### [3.2.0](https://github.com/Ousret/charset_normalizer/compare/3.1.0...3.2.0) (2023-06-07)
- Typehint for function `from_path` no longer enforce `PathLike` as its first argument [32]
- Minor improvement over the global detection reliability [32]

### [3.1.0](https://github.com/Ousret/charset_normalizer/compare/3.0.1...3.1.0) (2023-03-06)
- Argument `should_rename_legacy` for legacy function `detect` and disregard any new arguments without errors (PR #262) [33]

### [3.0.1](https://github.com/Ousret/charset_normalizer/compare/3.0.0...3.0.1) (2022-11-18)
- Multi-bytes cutter/chunk generator did not always cut correctly (PR #233) [34]

### [3.0.0](https://github.com/Ousret/charset_normalizer/compare/2.1.1...3.0.0) (2022-10-20)
- Extend the capability of explain=True when cp_isolation contains at most two entries (min one), will log in details of the Mess-detector results [11]
- Support for alternative language frequency set in charset_normalizer.assets.FREQUENCIES [11]
- Build with static metadata using 'build' frontend [12]
- Make the language detection stricter [12]
- Optional: Module `md.py` can be compiled using Mypyc to provide an extra speedup up to 4x faster than v2.1 [12]

### [3.0.0rc1](https://github.com/Ousret/charset_normalizer/compare/3.0.0b2...3.0.0rc1) (2022-10-18)
- Extend the capability of explain=True when cp_isolation contains at most two entries (min one), will log in details of the Mess-detector results [35]
- Support for alternative language frequency set in … [35]

### [3.0.0b2](https://github.com/Ousret/charset_normalizer/compare/3.0.0b1...3.0.0b2) (2022-08-21)
- `normalizer --version` now specify if current version provide extra speedup (meaning mypyc compilation whl) [36]

### [2.1.1](https://github.com/Ousret/charset_normalizer/compare/2.1.0...2.1.1) (2022-08-19)
- Function `normalize` scheduled for removal in 3.0 [37].

### [2.1.0](https://github.com/Ousret/charset_normalizer/compare/2.0.12...2.1.0) (2022-06-19)
- Output the Unicode table version when running the CLI with `--version` (PR #194)
- Reuse decoded buffer for single byte character sets from [@nijel] (PR #175)
- Fixing some performance bottlenecks [38]

### [2.0.12](https://github.com/Ousret/charset_normalizer/compare/2.0.11...2.0.12) (2022-02-12)
- ASCII miss-detection on rare cases (PR #170)
- Explicit support for Python 3.11 (PR #164)
- The logging behavior have been completely reviewed, now using only TRACE and DEBUG levels (PR #163 #165) [39]

### [2.0.11](https://github.com/Ousret/charset_normalizer/compare/2.0.10...2.0.11) (2022-01-30)
- Explicit support for Python 3.11 (PR #164)
- The logging behavior have been completely reviewed, now using only TRACE and DEBUG levels (PR #163 #165)
- Fixing fallback match entries that might lead to UnicodeDecodeError for large bytes sequence (PR #154) [40]

### [2.0.10](https://github.com/Ousret/charset_normalizer/compare/2.0.9...2.0.10) (2022-01-04)
- Fallback match entries might lead to UnicodeDecodeError for large bytes sequence (PR #154)
- Skipping the language-detection (CD) on ASCII (PR #155)
- Moderating the logging impact (since 2.0.8) for specific environments [41]

### [2.0.9](https://github.com/Ousret/charset_normalizer/compare/2.0.8...2.0.9) (2021-12-03)
- Moderating the logging impact (since 2.0.8) for specific environments (PR #147)
- Wrong logging level applied when setting kwarg `explain` to True (PR #146)
- Improvement over Vietnamese detection (PR #126) [42]

### [2.0.8](https://github.com/Ousret/charset_normalizer/compare/2.0.7...2.0.8) (2021-11-24)
- Improvement over Vietnamese detection (PR #126)
- MD improvement on trailing data and long foreign (non-pure latin) data (PR #124)
- Efficiency improvements in cd/alphabet_languages from [@adbar] (PR #122) [43]

### [2.0.7](https://github.com/Ousret/charset_normalizer/compare/2.0.6...2.0.7) (2021-10-11)
- Add support for Kazakh (Cyrillic) language detection (PR #109)
- Further, improve inferring the language from a given single-byte code page (PR #112)
- Vainly trying to leverage PEP263 when PEP3120 is not supported (PR #116) [44]

### [2.0.6](https://github.com/Ousret/charset_normalizer/compare/2.0.5...2.0.6) (2021-09-18)
- Unforeseen regression with the loss of the backward-compatibility with some older minor of Python 3.5.x (PR #100)
- Fix CLI crash when using --minimal output in certain cases (PR #103)
- Minor improvement to the detection [45]

### [2.0.5](https://github.com/Ousret/charset_normalizer/compare/2.0.4...2.0.5) (2021-09-14)
- The project now comply with: flake8, mypy, isort and black to ensure a better overall quality (PR #81)
- The BC-support with v1.x was improved, the old staticmethods are restored (PR #82)
- The Unicode detection is slightly improved [46]

### [2.0.1](https://github.com/Ousret/charset_normalizer/compare/2.0.0...2.0.1) (2021-07-13)
- Public function normalize default args values were not aligned with from_bytes (PR #53)
- You may now use charset aliases in cp_isolation and cp_exclusion arguments (PR #47)
- 4x to 5 times faster than the previous 1.4.0 release. At least 2x faster than Chardet.
- Accent has been made on UTF-8 detection, should perform rather instantaneous.
- The backward compatibility with Chardet has been greatly improved. The legacy detect function returns an identical charset name whenever possible.
- The detection mechanism has been slightly improved, now Turkish content is detected correctly (most of the time)
- The program has been rewritten to ease the readability and maintainability. (+Using static typing)+ [6]

### Pydantic Logfire :fire:
- We've launched Pydantic Logfire to help you monitor your applications. [15]

### Pydantic V1.10 vs. V2
- Pydantic V2 is a ground-up rewrite that offers many new features, performance improvements, and some breaking changes compared to Pydantic V1. [16]

### Help
- See the documentation for more details. [17]

### Installation
- Install using `pip install -U pydantic` or `conda install pydantic -c conda-forge`. For more installation options, see the documentation. [18]

### A Simple Example
- A code example is provided showing how to use Pydantic to define a `User` model with fields like `id`, `name`, `signup_ts`, and `friends`. [19]

### Contributing
- Guidance on setting up a development environment and making a contribution to Pydantic is available in the documentation. [20]

### Reporting a Security Vulnerability
- Information on how to report a security vulnerability can be found in the security policy. [21]

- The changelog section is empty or not filled out. [22]
